chunks: I asked him about a man who prays two rakʿahs of the witr and forgets the third until morning comes. He said: “He should perform the witr with one rakʿah when morning comes, at that very time.”
Saʿd, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Maymūn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj, who said:

I wrote to al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام asking him about some issues, and he wrote back to me: “Pray after al-ʿaṣr of the nawāfil whatever you wish, and pray after al-ghadāh of the nawāfil whatever you wish.”

key_terms.الثَّالِثَةَ: the third rakʿah that was forgotten
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title used for the Imam عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning time after the dawn prayer
key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the witr prayer, here referring to the final odd-numbered prayer unit
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs already performed in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the third rakʿah of witr until morning, and can nawāfil be prayed after al-ʿaṣr and al-ghadāh?
ai.summary: This hadith text addresses rulings related to supererogatory prayer, especially the witr and nawāfil performed after certain times. It indicates that if the third rakʿah of witr is forgotten until morning, it may be performed then, and it also permits praying nawāfil after al-ʿaṣr and after al-ghadāh.
